Possible personal-data exposure | Privacy / compliance reviewer | Limit disclosure and preserve incident evidence. | Information involved, discovery time, recipients and actions taken. Legal notice or litigation threat | Legal / compliance reviewer | Do not draft final legal position. | Correspondence reference and relevant history. Regulator correspondence | Compliance reviewer | Preserve attachment/version and audit trail. | Regulator, date, reference and complaint link. Accessibility barrier or accommodation request | Responsible service/human reviewer | Preserve request exactly; do not infer condition. | Requested channel or accommodation and impact. Potential vulnerability expressly described | Human reviewer | Do not diagnose or profile. | Exact customer statement and service impact. Conflicting current policies | Policy owner / compliance | Surface both sources; no automated resolution. | Source IDs, versions and conflicting passages.

This standard defines when a complaint remains with an analyst, when supervisor approval is required, and when specialist or senior escalation is mandatory. It separates the amount or impact described by a customer from a proposed bank action. Mentioning a large disputed transaction does not itself authorize compensation, closure or account action.

• Approve: records scope and authorized parameters. • Reject: records reason and returns case for revision or alternative handling. • Request more information: records missing evidence and leaves action disabled. • Escalate: routes to a higher or specialist authority while preserving prior review. • No response: remains pending; the system does not assume approval.

retrieval.query: How should a disputed fee be investigated?

results.text: This standard defines when a complaint remains with an analyst, when supervisor approval is required, and when specialist or senior escalation is mandatory. It separates the amount or impact described by a customer from a proposed bank action. Mentioning a large disputed transaction does not itself authorize compensation, closure or account action.

• Resolution documentation states the complaint understood, evidence reviewed, approved conclusion, action taken or proposed, any limitations, and next steps. • Policy claims must cite current approved sources. Operational facts must identify approved data-tool evidence. • Communication should be clear, respectful and accessible. It should not overstate certainty, legal authority or system capability. • When evidence is insufficient, explain what is missing and the manual next step rather than producing a likely answer. • Compensation language is prepared only after applicable approval. The amount disputed by a customer is not automatically a compensation recommendation.
No. Disputed transaction value and proposed compensation are different concepts. Authoritative reference: KB-002 §3
